paragraphs.text: For the law having a shadow of the good [things] to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect them that draw nigh.
paragraphs.original: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων, κατʼ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι·
paragraphs.translit: Skian gar echōn ho nomos tōn mellontōn agathōn, ouk autēn tēn eikona tōn pragmatōn, katʼ eniauton tais autais thysiais has prospherousin eis to diēnekes oudepote dynatai tous proserchomenous teleiōsai·

paragraphs.text: Else would they not have ceased to be offered? because the worshippers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins.
paragraphs.original: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι, διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ κεκαθαρισμένους;
paragraphs.translit: epei ouk an epausanto prospheromenai, dia to mēdemian echein eti syneidēsin hamartiōn tous latreuontas hapax kekatharismenous;

paragraphs.text: But in those [sacrifices] there is a remembrance made of sins year by year.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατʼ ἐνιαυτόν,
paragraphs.translit: allʼ en autais anamnēsis hamartiōn katʼ eniauton,

paragraphs.text: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
paragraphs.original: ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
paragraphs.translit: adynaton gar haima taurōn kai tragōn aphairein hamartias.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, But a body didst thou prepare for me;
paragraphs.original: διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει· Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι·
paragraphs.translit: dio eiserchomenos eis ton kosmon legei· Thysian kai prosphoran ouk ēthelēsas, sōma de katērtisō moi·

paragraphs.text: In whole burnt offerings and [sacrifices] for sin thou       hadst no pleasure:
paragraphs.original: ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας.
paragraphs.translit: holokautōmata kai peri hamartias ouk eudokēsas.

paragraphs.text: Then said I, Lo, I am come (In the roll of the book it is       written of me) To do thy will, O God.
paragraphs.original: τότε εἶπον· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω, ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου.
paragraphs.translit: tote eipon· Idou hēkō, en kephalidi bibliou gegraptai peri emou, tou poiēsai, ho theos, to thelēma sou.

paragraphs.text: Saying above, Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and [sacrifices] for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein (the which are offered according to the law),
paragraphs.original: ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ νόμον προσφέρονται,
paragraphs.translit: anōteron legōn hoti Thysias kai prosphoras kai holokautōmata kai peri hamartias ouk ēthelēsas oude eudokēsas, haitines kata nomon prospherontai,

paragraphs.text: then hath he said, Lo, I am come to do thy will. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
paragraphs.original: τότε εἴρηκεν· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου· ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: tote eirēken· Idou hēkō tou poiēsai to thelēma sou· anairei to prōton hina to deuteron stēsē.

paragraphs.text: By which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ.
paragraphs.translit: en hō thelēmati hēgiasmenoi esmen dia tēs prosphoras tou sōmatos Iēsou Christou ephapax.

paragraphs.text: And every priest indeed standeth day by day ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, the which can never take away sins:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθʼ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας, αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
paragraphs.translit: Kai pas men hiereus hestēken kathʼ hēmeran leitourgōn kai tas autas pollakis prospherōn thysias, haitines oudepote dynantai perielein hamartias.

paragraphs.text: but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;
paragraphs.original: οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: houtos de mian hyper hamartiōn prosenenkas thysian eis to diēnekes ekathisen en dexia tou theou,

paragraphs.text: henceforth expecting till his enemies be made the footstool of his feet.
paragraphs.original: τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: to loipon ekdechomenos heōs tethōsin hoi echthroi autou hypopodion tōn podōn autou,

paragraphs.text: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
paragraphs.original: μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.
paragraphs.translit: mia gar prosphora teteleiōken eis to diēnekes tous hagiazomenous.

paragraphs.text: And the Holy Spirit also beareth witness to us; for after he hath said,
paragraphs.original: μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εἰρηκέναι·
paragraphs.translit: martyrei de hēmin kai to pneuma to hagion, meta gar to eirēkenai·

paragraphs.text: This is the covenant that I will make with them After those days, saith the Lord: I will put my laws on their heart, And upon their mind also will I write them;     [then saith he,]
paragraphs.original: Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει κύριος, διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς,
paragraphs.translit: Hautē hē diathēkē hēn diathēsomai pros autous meta tas hēmeras ekeinas, legei kyrios, didous nomous mou epi kardias autōn, kai epi tēn dianoian autōn epigrapsō autous,

paragraphs.text: And their sins and their iniquities will I remember no       more.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ μνησθήσομαι ἔτι·
paragraphs.translit: kai tōn hamartiōn autōn kai tōn anomiōn autōn ou mē mnēsthēsomai eti·

paragraphs.text: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων, οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας.
paragraphs.translit: hopou de aphesis toutōn, ouketi prosphora peri hamartias.

paragraphs.text: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
paragraphs.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν, ἀδελφοί, παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Echontes oun, adelphoi, parrēsian eis tēn eisodon tōn hagiōn en tō haimati Iēsou,

paragraphs.text: by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
paragraphs.original: ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hēn enekainisen hēmin hodon prosphaton kai zōsan dia tou katapetasmatos, toutʼ estin tēs sarkos autou,

paragraphs.text: and [having] a great priest over the house of God;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai hierea megan epi ton oikon tou theou,

paragraphs.text: let us draw near with a true heart in fulness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience: and having our body washed with pure water,
paragraphs.original: προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως, ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ·
paragraphs.translit: proserchōmetha meta alēthinēs kardias en plērophoria pisteōs, rherantismenoi tas kardias apo syneidēseōs ponēras kai lelousmenoi to sōma hydati katharō·

paragraphs.text: let us hold fast the confession of our hope that it waver not; for he is faithful that promised:
paragraphs.original: κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ, πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος·
paragraphs.translit: katechōmen tēn homologian tēs elpidos aklinē, pistos gar ho epangeilamenos·

paragraphs.text: and let us consider one another to provoke unto love and good works;
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων,
paragraphs.translit: kai katanoōmen allēlous eis paroxysmon agapēs kai kalōn ergōn,

paragraphs.text: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting [one another]; and so much the more, as ye see the day drawing nigh.
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν, καθὼς ἔθος τισίν, ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν.
paragraphs.translit: mē enkataleipontes tēn episynagōgēn heautōn, kathōs ethos tisin, alla parakalountes, kai tosoutō mallon hosō blepete engizousan tēn hēmeran.

paragraphs.text: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more a sacrifice for sins,
paragraphs.original: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία,
paragraphs.translit: Hekousiōs gar hamartanontōn hēmōn meta to labein tēn epignōsin tēs alētheias, ouketi peri hamartiōn apoleipetai thysia,

paragraphs.text: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which shall devour the adversaries.
paragraphs.original: φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους.
paragraphs.translit: phobera de tis ekdochē kriseōs kai pyros zēlos esthiein mellontos tous hypenantious.

paragraphs.text: A man that hath set at nought Moses law dieth without compassion on [the word of] two or three witnesses:
paragraphs.original: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνῄσκει·
paragraphs.translit: athetēsas tis nomon Mōyseōs chōris oiktirmōn epi dysin ē trisin martysin apothnēskei·

paragraphs.text: of how much sorer punishment, think ye, shall he be judged worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant wherewith he was sanctified an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
paragraphs.original: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας, καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.
paragraphs.translit: posō dokeite cheironos axiōthēsetai timōrias ho ton hyion tou theou katapatēsas, kai to haima tēs diathēkēs koinon hēgēsamenos en hō hēgiasthē, kai to pneuma tēs charitos enybrisas.

paragraphs.text: For we know him that said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
paragraphs.original: οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω· καὶ πάλιν· Κρινεῖ κύριος τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: oidamen gar ton eiponta· Emoi ekdikēsis, egō antapodōsō· kai palin· Krinei kyrios ton laon autou.

paragraphs.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
paragraphs.original: φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας θεοῦ ζῶντος.
paragraphs.translit: phoberon to empesein eis cheiras theou zōntos.

paragraphs.text: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were enlightened, ye endured a great conflict of sufferings;
paragraphs.original: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας, ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων,
paragraphs.translit: Anamimnēskesthe de tas proteron hēmeras, en hais phōtisthentes pollēn athlēsin hypemeinate pathēmatōn,

paragraphs.text: partly, being made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, becoming partakers with them that were so used.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι, τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες·
paragraphs.translit: touto men oneidismois te kai thlipsesin theatrizomenoi, touto de koinōnoi tōn houtōs anastrephomenōn genēthentes·

paragraphs.text: For ye both had compassion on them that were in bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of you possessions, knowing that ye have for yourselves a better possession and an abiding one.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar tois desmiois synepathēsate, kai tēn harpagēn tōn hyparchontōn hymōn meta charas prosedexasthe, ginōskontes echein heautous kreittona hyparxin kai menousan.

paragraphs.text: Cast not away therefore your boldness, which hath great recompense of reward.
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἔχει μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν,
paragraphs.translit: mē apobalēte oun tēn parrēsian hymōn, hētis echei megalēn misthapodosian,

paragraphs.text: For ye have need of patience, that, having done the will of God, ye may receive the promise.
paragraphs.original: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν·
paragraphs.translit: hypomonēs gar echete chreian hina to thelēma tou theou poiēsantes komisēsthe tēn epangelian·

paragraphs.text: For yet a very little while, He that cometh shall come, and shall not tarry.
paragraphs.original: ἔτι γὰρ μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει·
paragraphs.translit: eti gar mikron hoson hoson, ho erchomenos hēxei kai ou chronisei·

paragraphs.text: But my righteous one shall live by faith: And if he shrink back, my soul hath no pleasure in him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de dikaios mou ek pisteōs zēsetai, kai ean hyposteilētai, ouk eudokei hē psychē mou en autō.

paragraphs.text: But we are not of them that shrink back unto perdition; but of them that have faith unto the saving of the soul.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν, ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de ouk esmen hypostolēs eis apōleian, alla pisteōs eis peripoiēsin psychēs.
